data.text: Caching reduces database load and improves response times. Hot Chocolate supports field-level caching, query caching, and distributed caching.
Use `[UseCache]` on query methods to cache the result. The cache key is based on the query arguments.

data.title: Cache a Query
data.content: Cache book lookup by ID for 5 minutes.

data.text: For full query results, use `[UseQueryCache]`. This is useful for expensive aggregations or reports.

data.title: Query Cache
data.content: Cache a stats query for 1 minute.

data.text: For multi-server deployments, use a distributed cache like Redis. Hot Chocolate works with any `IMemoryCache` or `IDistributedCache` implementation.

data.title: Cache Invalidation
data.text: Cache invalidation is the hardest part of caching. Use tags or time-based expiration, and always invalidate related caches when data changes.

terms.definition: Caches the result of a single resolver field.
Caches the entire result of a query operation.
A cache shared across multiple server instances, typically Redis.

data.title: Key Takeaways
data.takeaway: Next, we'll limit expensive queries with complexity analysis.
